# Notch So Good

> Peek, a tiny 3D character, lives in your MacBook's notch and watches your AI coding agents (Claude Code and OpenAI Codex CLI) so you don't have to.

## What it is

Notch So Good is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app for developers who run AI coding agents. While an agent works, a black pill extends the notch with Peek (a real-time 3D character rendered in Metal) and a ring showing how much of your 5-hour usage window is left. When an agent needs you (a question, a permission, a finished task) the notch opens into a card. Click it to jump back to the exact terminal tab.

## Key features

- Session pill: Dynamic Island-style pill with Peek, a usage ring, and a per-session list on hover (each session has its own colour, task name and timer)
- Peek has idle life (breathing, blinks, glances) and reacts to state: working, thinking, needs you, done, error
- Permission approvals from the notch: the exact command, Allow / Always allow / Deny, global hotkeys Ctrl-Opt-A / Ctrl-Opt-D. It only approves after a click; everything else is left to the agent's own permission rules, and chained shell commands never ride on an allow rule
- Permission-mode aware: no prompt in bypass, auto or plan mode
- Usage: 5-hour and weekly limits for Claude Code and Codex, reset times, pace forecast, heads-ups at 80% and 95%
- Task names taken from your prompt, session identity colours, jump to the right terminal tab and display
- Eight finishes for Peek: Obsidian, Chrome, Gold, Holo, Neon, Porcelain, Gummy, Frosted
- Light on resources: frames that would not change are not drawn; idles at a couple of percent of one core
- Launch at login, auto-update notices via Sparkle

## Install

brew install --cask deepshal99/tap/notch-so-good

Or: npx notch-so-good

Or: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/deepshal99/notch-so-good/main/get.sh | bash

## Requirements

- macOS 14+ (Sonoma or later)
- Claude Code or OpenAI Codex CLI
- A MacBook with a notch is best; works without one too

## How it works

Claude Code / Codex hooks run a small Python bridge (~/.notchsogood/hook.py) that sends events over a local Unix domain socket (/tmp/notchsogood.sock, owner-only) the app listens on. Every event carries the agent's live permission_mode. Permission checks are bidirectional: the hook waits for your answer from the notch. Usage limits are read from your own local logins (Claude Code's OAuth credentials in the Keychain, Codex CLI's ~/.codex/auth.json). No server, no accounts, nothing leaves your Mac.
